gaps.sentence: The hotel, ___ rates include breakfast, is fully booked for the conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' marks possession even for things: the hotel whose rates…

gaps.sentence: Our new neighbours, ___ have three children, moved in last week.
gaps.hint: people as subject; clause between commas
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is used for people in non-defining clauses; 'which' is for things.

gaps.sentence: My uncle, ___ lives in Canada, is coming to stay next week.
gaps.hint: non-defining clause after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses (between commas) 'that' is not allowed; 'who' refers to people.

gaps.sentence: July and August are the months ___ most Italians take their holidays.
gaps.explanation: 'When' means 'in which' after time expressions; the clause describes when the action happens.

gaps.sentence: 1998 was the year ___ the factory finally closed.
That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: The girl ___ sits behind me in class is from Peru.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to a person who is the subject; 'which' refers only to things.

gaps.sentence: The house ___ windows were broken has now been sold.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose windows' — the windows belong to the house.
